title: Accessing and Modifying Array Values
objectives: Read values from arrays using indexes.
theory: Reading an array element uses the index. int firstScore = scores[0]; reads the first element. Console.WriteLine(weapons[2]); prints the third element.
Changing an array element uses assignment. scores[0] = 95; replaces the first element with 95. inventory[2] = "Key"; changes the third inventory item.
Index boundaries are critical. An array of size 5 has valid indices 0 through 4. Accessing scores[5] is out of bounds and causes an IndexOutOfRangeException.
The .Length property tells you the array size. scores.Length returns 5 for an array of 5 elements. Use it to prevent index errors: if (i < scores.Length)
Common mistakes include forgetting zero-based indexing, accessing beyond array bounds, and confusing index numbers. Always verify indices are within 0 to length−1.
tryIt: Create an array, modify a value, and print it before and after the change.
challenge: Create an array and verify the index is valid before accessing each element.
mistakes: Index out of bounds causes exceptions.
Always verify before accessing unfamiliar indices.
summary: Access array elements using indexes within bounds. Modify with assignment. Use .Length to check validity. Index errors are a common source of bugs.
